content.content:
usage: gnd discover [-h] --out OUT --report REPORT --actor ACTOR
                    --requested-at REQUESTED_AT [--families FAMILIES]
                    [--max-values MAX_VALUES] [--max-pairs MAX_PAIRS]
                    [--min-support MIN_SUPPORT] [--show-values]
                    [--type-evidence PATH] [--type-evidence-in PATH]
                    [--duplicate-judgements PATH] [--shape-judgements PATH]
                    [--joined-relation FACT:SOURCE:TARGET]
                    [--joined-classifier FACT:ENTITY:CLASS]
                    [--joined-marker FACT:ENTITY:VALUE=JSON]
                    [--max-directed-pairs N] [--format {text,json}]
                    model population

Propose candidate constraints of seven families (uniqueness, mandatory, value,
frequency, subset, equality, exclusion) that hold in one population. A
candidate is kept only when `gnd check` passes it with support > 0 and the
model neither declares nor entails it. Writes a discovery report and, when
anything is emitted, a `gnd evolve` proposal of induced, proposed, deontic
constraints: admission stays a reviewed act. Exits 0 on success (also with
nothing emitted), 3 on an invalid model or population, 11 when --out already
exists (nothing written), 64 on a usage error, 66 on a missing input or
reference file, 70 on an internal defect, 74 on a refused output or reference
path.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model file
  population            path to the population file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out OUT             write the evolve proposal here
  --report REPORT       write the discovery report here
  --actor ACTOR         who requests the proposal (its audit actor_id)
  --requested-at REQUESTED_AT
                        when, as ISO-8601 with a UTC offset (the audit time;
                        keeps output reproducible)
  --families FAMILIES   comma-separated subset of the seven default families;
                        add fact-type or guarded-join to opt in
  --max-values MAX_VALUES
                        largest distinct-value count for a value candidate
                        (default 20)
  --max-pairs MAX_PAIRS
                        most unordered role pairs compared for
                        subset/equality/exclusion (default 256)
  --min-support MIN_SUPPORT
                        fact-type family: fewest distinct entities for a
                        proposal (default 20)
  --show-values         fact-type family: also report each attribute value as
                        text (disclosure mode decides)
  --type-evidence PATH  fact-type family: also write the evidence the
                        judgement skills read
  --type-evidence-in PATH
                        fact-type family: the evidence file the judgements
                        bind
  --duplicate-judgements PATH
                        fact-type family: read duplicate verdicts (needs
                        --type-evidence-in)
  --shape-judgements PATH
                        fact-type family: read multi-valued shape verdicts
                        (needs --type-evidence-in)
  --joined-relation FACT:SOURCE:TARGET
                        guarded-join family: binary relation and endpoint
                        roles
  --joined-classifier FACT:ENTITY:CLASS
                        guarded-join family: binary classifier and its roles
  --joined-marker FACT:ENTITY:VALUE=JSON
                        guarded-join family: restrict same-class candidates by
                        a target marker
  --max-directed-pairs N
                        guarded-join family: most ordered class pairs
                        considered (default 256)
  --format {text,json}  output rendering: human-readable text (default) or one
                        JSON payload

BLOCKING (alethic)
  (none)
ADVISORY (deontic)
  (none)
pass=2 fail=0 warning=0 unchecked=0 vacuous=0
COVERAGE
  refund_by: declared, facts=3
  refund_amount: declared, facts=3
  refund_channel: declared, facts=3

I've read the inputs, and nothing has been written yet. Before I run discovery, I need two answers from you.

**What I'll run:** `gnd discover` on `model.orm.yaml` and `batches/south.yaml`, with `--families uniqueness,mandatory`. That covers your two kinds: "each X has exactly one Y" (uniqueness) and "every X has a Y" (mandatory).

**What I already checked (read-only):** `gnd check` passes both of south's constraints (`pass=2 fail=0`). South has 3 refunds, and each refund has a customer, an amount and a channel.

**Questions:**

1. **Who should the proposal be recorded as?** This becomes the audit actor on the proposal. Give me a name or identifier.
2. **At what time?** An ISO-8601 timestamp with a UTC offset, for example `2026-11-26T09:00:00+00:00`.

**One thing to know about output names:** `discovered.json` already exists in this folder as an empty file. Discover refuses an existing `--out`, so I'd write to `proposal.json` and `discovery-report.json` here instead. Tell me if you want different names.

Once you answer, I'll run discovery and read every candidate back to you in plain English. Because south is a single week of only 3 refunds, expect some accidental rules; you'll decide which ones are real.
